prompt:
Create exactly one high-fidelity 16:9 landscape desktop WEBSITE UI MOCKUP for VEEMAP Technologies, card direction “The Metrology Dossier”. This must look like a shippable premium industrial-engineering homepage first viewport captured in a browser, NOT a poster, not concept art, not a photograph with overlaid copy.

STRUCTURE AND READING ORDER:
1) A restrained thin top navigation on optical white: at far left the wordmark “VEEMAP” in graphite with a small abstract chevron mark derived from the supplied logo’s orange and green geometry; centered/right compact nav labels “CAPABILITIES”, “SYSTEMS”, “PROJECTS”, “CAREERS”; at far right one small text link “CONTACT”.
2) Main canvas below nav uses an asymmetrical editorial metrology layout. Left 38% is a disciplined text column on measurement paper. Right/center 52% is the dominant hero object: a precise, conceptually accurate, NON-PROPRIETARY high-speed pick-and-place mechanism floating in oblique three-quarter view over a technical coordinate field. The mechanism has satin aluminium arms, linear rails, a compact gripper, sensor/vision head, optical inspection glass, realistic fasteners and joints, but NO customer-specific detail and no recognizable proprietary machine.
3) The hero mechanism is the single dominant focal moment. Optical blue scan light slices through part of the assembly. A sparse coordinate field and hairline metrology axes sit behind it, with no blueprint cliché.
4) Place EXACTLY THREE and only three decisive measurement/capability callouts connected by precise hairlines to the mechanism. Their exact labels are:
“VISION-GUIDED INSPECTION”
“HIGH-SPEED PICK + PLACE”
“PREDICTIVE MACHINE HEALTH”
Do not add any other callout, badge, tolerance, decimal, percentage, dimension, machine metric, or invented number.
5) A very narrow vertical evidence rail along the far right edge, visually integrated rather than a card stack. It contains exactly these two sourced facts, clearly typeset:
“236 PROJECTS DELIVERED”
“55 CLIENTS”
Do not invent additional metrics.
6) Bottom-left primary action is a strong engineered rectangular control with exact copy “START A REQUIREMENT REVIEW”, metrology blue fill, optical white text, a small VEEMAP-orange registration notch; it must clearly read as the primary button.
7) Under the headline or aligned beside it, include the exact supporting line “Mechanisms, controls and intelligence engineered around your process.”

REQUIRED PRIMARY COPY, reproduce verbatim and legibly:
“VEEMAP”
“ACCURACY AT SPEED.”
“Mechanisms, controls and intelligence engineered around your process.”
“START A REQUIREMENT REVIEW”
“236 PROJECTS DELIVERED”
“55 CLIENTS”

VISUAL WORLD:
Optical white #F4F7F8 is dominant, graphite #172027 for text and hardware depth, metrology blue #1754D1 for scan light and primary action, VEEMAP orange #FF982E as a precise registration accent, fluorescent inspection lime #B9FF37 used very sparingly for one active datum/status trace. Materials: inspection glass, satin aluminium, crisp measurement paper, optical scan light. Typography: premium condensed industrial grotesk for the headline, precise neutral sans for interface and annotations; emphatic scale but no text larger than the mechanism. Strong whitespace, razor-sharp alignment, realistic UI density, subtle surface shadows with offset and blur, meticulous production polish.

REFERENCE IMAGE:
Use the supplied VEEMAP logo only as reference for the small orange/green chevron mark and color relationship. Preserve the recognizable double-chevron geometry in a simplified top-left mark. Do not reproduce the logo as a huge image and do not use its white JPEG background as a panel.

MOBILE-AWARE IMPLICATION:
Although this image is desktop 16:9, keep semantic sections and a clear hierarchy that could stack cleanly on mobile; no microscopic essential controls.

STRICT AVOID:
generic SaaS cards, bento dashboard cards, black neon cyberpunk, dark hero background, decorative blueprint grid cliché, fake tolerances, fake numbers, invented claims, proprietary machine details, client logos, people, humans, watermarks, social media chrome, browser device frame, poster composition, illegible pseudo-text, decorative glassmorphism, excessive rounded pills, excessive gradients. Exactly one homepage viewport, no montage.
